PATCH /api/buildings/:id/escalation-profile mutates building.escalationProfile for any building by :id with only a role check; sibling PATCH /api/buildings/:id (line 167) enforces managerCanAccessBuilding, which is missing here, so a manager can reconfigure escalation policy of buildings they don't manage.

POST /api/buildings/:id/lobby-kiosk/pairing-code issues a kiosk pairing code (issueKioskPairingCode(id)) for any building by :id with only a role check and no managerCanAccessBuilding predicate, letting a manager pair kiosks to buildings outside their assigned portfolio.

POST /api/inspections creates an inspection under an attacker-supplied unitId with only a role check and no managerCanAccessBuilding check on the unit's building, so a property_manager can create inspections for units outside their scope (create under attacker-selected parent).

PATCH /api/inspections/:id updates any inspection (status/findings/recommendations/tenantVisible) selected by :id with only a role check. No managerCanAccessBuilding predicate (sibling site-photo route line 135 enforces it), so a property_manager can edit inspections in buildings outside their scope.

Protected data is written to durable storage without encryption or hashing: 'routingNumber' is passed straight into the persistence call without encryption.

POST /api/leases/:id/move-out-notice writes move-out notice into any lease's notes via fileLeaseMoveOutNotice(repo,id,...). Unlike sibling autopay (line 245), move-out-packet (line 272) and move-out-packet-safe (line 287), there is no `tenantId !== req.user.id` ownership check and no role guard, so any authenticated user can modify any lease.

PATCH /api/messages/:id/read updates any message by attacker-controlled :id with no check that the caller is sender or recipient; sibling GET /api/messages scopes by req.user.id, so cross-user read-state mutation is possible.

PATCH /api/notifications/:id/read updates any notification by :id without binding it to req.user.id; sibling /read-all correctly scopes by userId, and GET /api/notifications scopes by user, so any authenticated user can mutate another user's notification.

An HTTP response discloses data the caller is not entitled to receive: When view=internal, the catch block sends err.stack in the HTTP response, exposing an internal stack trace with no redaction or field narrowing.

GET /api/tickets/descriptions-search has no preHandler and no tenant scoping; searchTicketDescriptionsByTerm queries every maintenance ticket's id/title/description globally, so any authenticated user (including a tenant) can read other tenants' ticket data by keyword, unlike GET /api/tickets which filters tenants.

This endpoint is configured with a plaintext http:// scheme and is used elsewhere to transmit a credential (API key, token, or password) as a query parameter or Authorization header, exposing it to any on-path observer.

POST /api/units creates a unit under an attacker-supplied buildingId with only a role check; no managerCanAccessBuilding check on the parent building, so a property_manager can create units in buildings they don't manage (create under attacker-selected parent).

POST /api/units/:id/listing-sync applies attacker body via applyListingSyncPayload(Object.assign) to any unit selected by :id. No managerCanAccessBuilding check (sibling PATCH /api/units/:id line 209 enforces it), so a property_manager can modify units in buildings they don't manage.

An AES-CBC decryption failure (invalid padding) is distinguishable from other failures through an externally observable response (branch), without a prior authentication/integrity check — a CBC padding oracle.

POST /api/units/:id/lockbox-sync writes a decrypted lockbox access code into any unit's description selected by :id with only a role check; no managerCanAccessBuilding predicate (sibling PATCH enforces it), so a manager can push lockbox codes into units outside their scope.
Fast unsalted sha256 digest used for password/credential material — use bcrypt/scrypt/argon2.

POST /api/users/:id/vendor-portal-access overwrites the passwordHash of any user by attacker-selected :id with sha256(accessCode) under only a role check; no managerCanAccessUser predicate (GET /api/users/:id enforces it), so a property_manager can corrupt/overwrite credentials of arbitrary users.

POST /api/users/:id/worker-app-pin lets a property_manager set a bcrypt password hash (provisionMaintenanceWorkerCredential) for ANY user by attacker-selected :id. No managerCanAccessUser/scope check (unlike GET /api/users/:id line 79), so a manager can overwrite the password of admins or other managers and log in as them.

`handler` completes an account-recovery/verification flow — issuing a session or writing a new password — without ever comparing the submitted proof against the stored secret. The account is selected by an attacker-supplied identifier alone, so anyone who knows the email address can take the account over. Compare the proof in constant time against the stored (hashed) value and require it to be unexpired and single-use.
